original_question: Fix 0 <= rho, mu, nu <= 1. If A,B subseteq R^n have Gaussian measures mu and nu respectively and A is centrally symmetric, A = -A, what is the minimum possible value of Pr[x in A, y in B] when (x,y) are rho-correlated n-dimensional Gaussian vectors?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's stated open problem very closely: it fixes 0 <= rho, mu, nu <= 1, takes A,B subseteq R^n with Gaussian measures mu and nu, assumes A is centrally symmetric, and asks for the minimum of Pr[X in A, Y in B] for rho-correlated n-dimensional Gaussian vectors. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
missing_details: Specify that the measure is the standard Gaussian measure gamma_n on R^n, and that A and B are measurable.
Quantify the dimension explicitly (for a fixed or arbitrary n >= 1); the paper states the problem in R^n but the draft leaves the quantifier on n implicit.
Define precisely what 'rho-correlated n-dimensional Gaussians' means, e.g. X,Z are independent N(0,I_n) and Y = rho X + sqrt(1-rho^2) Z, equivalently Cov(X_i,Y_j) = rho delta_ij.
State explicitly that the optimization is over all such measurable A,B with gamma_n(A)=mu and gamma_n(B)=nu.

If you want the paper's only explicit equivalent reformulation, note that it is equivalent to impose both A = -A and B = -B. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
refined_question: For fixed n >= 1 and 0 <= rho, mu, nu <= 1, let gamma_n denote the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. Among all measurable sets A,B subseteq R^n with gamma_n(A)=mu, gamma_n(B)=nu, and A=-A, determine the minimum possible value of P[X in A, Y in B], where X,Z are independent N(0,I_n) random vectors and Y = rho X + sqrt(1-rho^2) Z (equivalently, (X,Y) are standard rho-correlated n-dimensional Gaussian vectors).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation stated in the paper: impose both symmetries A = -A and B = -B, with the same Gaussian-measure constraints and the same minimization of P[X in A, Y in B].
justification: The draft clearly targets the unnumbered open problem titled "Symmetric Gaussian Problem" rather than a broader neighboring topic. The official statement on PDF page 8 is essentially the same question as your draft. The nearby remarks add the paper-faithful refinements that (i) one may equivalently require both A=-A and B=-B, (ii) without symmetry the minimizers are opposing halfspaces by Borell's result, and (iii) the centered-ball/complement-of-centered-ball claim is presented only as a reasonable conjecture, not as the formal problem statement, so it should not replace the question itself. The main improvements needed are only the stand-alone definitions of gamma_n, measurability, the quantifier on n, and the precise meaning of rho-correlation. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
